ADAR1 knockdown or expression of ADAR1G1119R and ADAR1P3A alleles pathogenic variants reduced adenosine-to-inosine RNA editing

statements.text: A-to-I RNA editing inhibits type I interferon signaling

excluded.reason: reduced editing and raised IFN-stimulated genes are two parallel outcomes of perturbing ADAR1 ('ADAR1 knockdown or expression of ... alleles ... reduced adenosine-to-inosine RNA editing and increased IFN-stimulated genes'); the text never says editing restrains IFN signalling, and the perturbation is of ADAR (which UniProt P55265 says also acts editing-independently via EIF2AK2/PKR), not of editing

statements.text: type I interferon signaling goes with psoriasis (higher IFN signalling in psoriasis)
statements.sign_note: the run's polarity is 'unknown'; the text it cited gives the direction: psoriasis families 'characterized by a strong IFN signature in skin and blood' (PMID:42424135)

evidence.quote: early-onset plaque psoriasis, with or without psoriatic arthritis, segregating as a monogenic trait and characterized by a strong IFN signature in skin and blood

hyp_ADAR_psoriasis.note: the title names ADAR loss-of-function variants, but the chain starts at the ADAR protein, so the claim is on ADAR with the sign inverted ('loss of ADAR drives psoriasis'). The title's 'interferon-dependent subtype of psoriasis' has no MONDO term; the chain ends at psoriasis (MONDO:0005083) and so does the claim.

findings.detail: Confidence 'low' and support 'speculative' understate the run's own citation: PMID:42424135 reports four heterozygous ADAR1 loss-of-function mutations cosegregating with psoriasis in four families, six more rare variants in 125 patients, and knockdown/allele experiments raising IFN-stimulated genes.

The title ('ADAR loss-of-function drives an interferon-dependent subtype of psoriasis') paraphrases the title of the one paper cited (PMID:42424135, 2026); the hypothesis is a retrieved finding, not a new one.

The proposed falsification (ADAR knockdown in keratinocytes, expect more type I IFN signalling) is essentially the experiment PMID:42424135 already reports ('ADAR1 knockdown ... increased IFN-stimulated genes'), so it would not test anything new.

The step gives polarity 'unknown' while the text it cites states the direction (a 'strong IFN signature in skin and blood', an 'IFN-dependent psoriasis subtype'); the curation takes the direction from the text.

The mechanism's key intermediate, accumulation of unedited endogenous dsRNA acting as an innate immune trigger, is neither a chain step nor stated by either cited text; the chain jumps from editing straight to IFN signalling.

The strongest evidence in the run, familial cosegregation of ADAR1 loss-of-function mutations with psoriasis (PMID:42424135), is not attached to any step: the chain only carries the mechanism, so the genetic link itself is never claimed as a step.

The run abstains on IFNW1 ('not detected' in HPA) and ZBP1, although the corpus UniProt records annotate IFNW1 (P05000) to type I interferon-mediated signaling pathway (GO:0060337) and ZBP1 (Q9H171) to its positive regulation (GO:0060340), the very node its only hypothesis runs through; absence of tissue expression is used as evidence of no role.

The abstention cites PMID:PPR1233591, GWAS:SP100:no-association, HPA:ENSG00000138472, HPA:ENSG00000138030 and HPA:ENSG00000177047; none is in sources.json, so its claims (e.g. PANoptosis in psoriasis is ZBP1-independent; zero GWAS variants for SP100) could not be checked.

Abstentions: the format has no place for a run's abstention statement or its citations, and sources.json omits them, although a GWAS null (SP100) or a ZBP1-independence result is exactly a refuting or 'none' association BioLean could hold.

Hypothesis-level evidence: the cited cosegregation result states the claim itself (ADAR loss → psoriasis), and the knockdown result states ADAR →− IFN-stimulated genes, but no step carries either, and a bridge is allowed only when an arm needs one to compose, so the arm's belief rests on the mechanism alone and ignores the best evidence.

The arm composes with the claimed sign (ADAR →− psoriasis risk) but gets belief 0, 'unsupported', because S2 (editing →− IFN signalling) has no evidence once the co-outcome span is excluded; even with it kept, steps at 5/6, 1/2 and 1/2 times the 1/5 fromAssoc weight give 1/24: the paper's end-to-end results (ADAR1 loss-of-function cosegregating with psoriasis; ADAR1 knockdown raising IFN-stimulated genes) cannot reach the arm.

PMID:42424135 reports two co-outcomes of one perturbation (ADAR1 knockdown 'reduced adenosine-to-inosine RNA editing and increased IFN-stimulated genes'); the guide does not say whether that states editing → IFN signalling. Excluded here (audit) under 'the text states the step': the perturbation is of ADAR, which UniProt P55265 says also acts editing-independently via suppression of EIF2AK2/PKR, so the span does not isolate editing.

The only citation for 'A-to-I RNA editing inhibits type I IFN signalling' (PMID:42424135) reports reduced editing and raised IFN-stimulated genes as parallel outcomes of ADAR1 knockdown or pathogenic alleles; it states ADAR1 loss → more ISGs, a link that skips editing, but never that editing restrains IFN signalling.

The mechanism says the type I IFN response 'drives' the psoriasis subtype, a causal, signed link, but the chain records the step as associated_with with polarity 'unknown', so the arm can only use it as an association (×1/5).

The span 'Functional studies showed that ADAR1 knockdown or expression of ... alleles' does not name its system; recorded as inVitro (knockdown, allele expression, drug reversal read as cell work), but the abstract does not say.

The only evidence for IFN signalling ↔ psoriasis comes from monogenic ADAR1-mutant families, a subtype; a refinement of psoriasis would break the chain, and evidence has no field to say its population is narrower than the claim's node.

No MONDO term for the 'interferon-dependent psoriasis subtype' the title names (MONDO has ADAR-related type 1 interferonopathy, MONDO:0700261, not a psoriasis subtype); no BLN term made because the chain ends at psoriasis.

audit.before: kept, inVitro: 'reduced adenosine-to-inosine RNA editing and increased IFN-stimulated genes'
audit.reason: the quote cuts off its subject ('ADAR1 knockdown or expression of ... alleles'): reduced editing and raised ISGs are parallel outcomes of perturbing ADAR, not a statement that editing restrains IFN signalling; ADAR also acts editing-independently (UniProt P55265, EIF2AK2/PKR). Guide example S2 is not a precedent: there the perturbed thing (RIDD) is part of the step's subject and the outcome is its object.
the step's only citation does not state it; that is a hypothesis-agent result
the mechanism says the IFN response 'drives' psoriasis, but step 3 is associated_with/unknown, which costs the arm the 1/5 fromAssoc weight

audit.reason: follows the S2 exclusion; the curator read 'discounted by four fifths' as x4/5, but assocWeight in BioLean/Derivation.lean is 1/5 for non-variants, which gives exactly 1/24
